## Recon: false-positive surface measured (read-only probe, 2026-08-20)

AST-scanned all 2,416 `.py` files under `scripts/` + `src/`; 0 parse failures; 584 distinct
import roots; 59 third-party after stdlib + naive first-party filtering. Against `uv.lock`
(226 dists) + `pyproject.toml` deps: 36 resolve by direct name, 6 need an import-name ->
dist-name mapping, 17 unresolved. The 17 split into three classes the plan must separate —
this is the whole difficulty of the task, and it is NOT visible from the body:

1. **First-party, package-style (455 of the sites!)** — `scripts` (402 sites, e.g.
   `from scripts.x import y`) and `src` (53 sites). These MUST resolve as first-party.
   A first-party resolver keyed only on module stems misses them entirely, which is how a
   naive implementation produces a 455-site false-positive avalanche.
2. **First-party, dangling** — `_issue506_common`, `analyze_issue396`, `issue500_predictors`,
   `issue541_personas`, `issue541_predictors`, `issue541_upload_lib`, `issue621_analyze`,
   `issue_521_prep_turner_corpus`, and probably `jlens`: local-module imports with no
   matching file in main (sibling modules living on unmerged issue branches, or deleted).
   Real latent breakage, but a DIFFERENT class from this task's Goal — the plan must decide
   explicitly whether to report them (recommend: separate WARN bucket, never conflated with
   the third-party verdict).
3. **Genuine third-party absent from the lockfile — the target class, ~6 roots:**
   `adjustText` (1 site), `math_verify` (1), `pingouin` (2), `sparsify` (2 — the very #2103
   incident), `speculators` (1), and `open_instruct` (7, which is the
   `external/open-instruct` working-tree overlay and needs a declared-overlay resolution
   path, not an allowlist). Each needs a recorded disposition before the check can ship
   FAIL-level bundled into no-flags, per acceptance criterion 3 ("reported rather than
   silently allowlisted").

## Two observations for the planner (scope-sharpening, Goal unchanged)

- **The check is branch-AGNOSTIC, which makes it strictly simpler and stronger than the
  body sketches.** An unresolvable import is a latent `ModuleNotFoundError` wherever it
  sits — production branch, smoke branch, or nested three helpers deep — because
  resolvability does not depend on reachability. So this check needs no smoke/production
  branch analysis at all, and thereby inherits NONE of the
  `--check-smoke-blind-spots` scanner's documented false negatives (one-level helper
  resolution, un-recursed `ast.Match` bodies, dynamic dispatch, non-`smoke`-named flags).
  A plain `ast.walk` satisfies acceptance criterion 2 (the #1336 nested-helper shape) for
  free. The only legitimate exemption is an import deliberately guarded by
  `try/except ImportError` on a non-load-bearing path.
- **`importlib.metadata.packages_distributions()` resolves all 6 measured
  import-name != dist-name cases with zero hand-maintenance** (PIL->pillow,
  dotenv->python-dotenv, hydra->hydra-core, sklearn->scikit-learn, umap->umap-learn,
  yaml->pyyaml). But it reads the LIVE venv, so a lint keyed on it is
  environment-dependent and would give different verdicts on a fresh pod. The body
  requires a table-driven, unit-tested mapping. Recommend the planner weigh a hybrid:
  static table as the deterministic primary, venv metadata as an optional cross-check that
  flags table drift, and a loud FAIL on any unmapped unknown (as the body specifies).
